To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the species richness, tree and stems density, basal area, and the recruitment pattern of tropical rain forests in the Western Ghats of India were monitored for ten (10) years, and that changes in the species richness and basal areas were observed in majority (60%) of the forest sites.
the species richness, basal area and density of stems and trees were found to vary with forest type.
the forest dynamics of the tropical rainforests of the study region are influenced by the forest type, physiognomy of the forests and the human activities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following aspects.
the dynamics of the tropical rain forest in Western Ghats in India.
the following aspects: (1) species richness (2) tree and stem density (3) basal area (4) regeneration (5) growth of trees and stems (6) mortality of trees and stems and (7) extraction pressure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the forest dynamics in the evergreen forests is towards the deciduous forest, and in the moist deciduous forest towards a degraded condition.
the forest dynamics in these tropical rain forests of the Western Ghats is a function of the physiognomic and floristic composition of the forests, the forest management and the forest use pattern.
the tropical rain forests of the Western Ghats are undergoing a dynamic state of vegetation change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, the forest dynamics of the tropical evergreen and moist tropical rain forests in the study area is a function of the physiognomic characteristics of the forest, site potentiality, and the human pressure on the forests.
the forest sites in ever green zone of the tropical rain forest are in good condition, while those in moist deciduous zone are deteriorating, with the former showing a trend towards a climax forest.
the forest dynamics in these forest sites are influenced by the site conditions, physiognomic composition and the extraction pressure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the forests of the Western Ghats, which are under pressure due to anthropogenic activities, are capable of recovering and retaining their physiognomy if protected and managed appropriately.
the tropical rain forests of this region are dynamic, and the dynamics of these forests is governed by the species richness and the physiognomic character of the forests.
forest management and conservation practices need to be adapted to suit the specific requirements of the forest type and the site conditions.
